TabPFN-3.5 Hackathon · tab-trader

TabPFN-3.5 on Kalshi's 15-minute Bitcoin markets

Real, messy, self-recorded market data (245 million rows since 2026-03-21). TabPFN decides which trades to take. One CPU, no training loop, no tuning.

Bottom line

  • It ranks my live strategy's signals best. In a weekly walk-forward (22 weeks, 2,905 signals), TabPFN-3.5 scores AUC 0.732, against 0.726 for logistic regression and 0.686 for LightGBM, with no tuning.
  • Its veto works on real fills. Of my 395 actual live trades since 2026-09-12, the 171 TabPFN would have kept earned +6.33¢ per contract; the rest earned -0.31¢. At 15% per trade, $100 ends at $655.25 with its veto, against $370.65 as I traded.
  • Public benchmark (generic indicators, rerunnable from this repo): 15-minute market: TabPFN-3.5 ranks #2 of 8 models on prediction error, significantly ahead of 5 of 6 tuned classic models; hourly ladder: TabPFN-3.5 has the lowest prediction error of 8 models, significantly ahead of 1 of 6 tuned classic models. Nothing beats the market price itself on prediction error.
  • The long walk-forward is a tough test. From 2026-05-11 to 2026-10-07, logistic regression with half-Kelly stakes finished highest ($12,269); TabPFN ends at $9,431 with half-Kelly stakes and $687.51 at a flat 15%. July decided it: my signal lost 4.65¢ per contract that month, and TabPFN, still learning from April to June, did not step aside.
  • One CPU, no tuning. A weekly refit takes under a minute; scoring a live signal about a second.

1. The strategy: TabPFN as a weekly-refit trade filter

The table and chart below show every filter, including the ones that beat TabPFN.

Private features. This section uses my live strategy's real signals and its own 32 features, which are not published. The repo contains each model's scores, decisions and outcomes, so the results can be checked. The public-data results (sections 2, 3 and 6) use only generic indicators.
  1. A momentum signal from my live strategy proposes a trade a few times an hour.
  2. Every Monday, TabPFN-3.5 reads the previous 12 weeks of signals and their outcomes as context. It is not trained or tuned.
  3. For each new signal it returns the probability of winning. The trade is taken only if that probability beats the entry price plus Kalshi's fee.
  4. Stake: a flat 15% of the account, or half the Kelly stake implied by TabPFN's probability, capped at 15%.

The same weekly refit and the same rule are applied to logistic regression and LightGBM. My current filter is a model trained once in spring and then frozen. The rules were written down before the test ran (PREREG.md, amendment 3).

Zoom: real fills since 2026-09-12

How to read the dollar figures. Each trade stakes 15% of the balance (or half-Kelly) but never more than 500 contracts, a stand-in for the depth of Kalshi's order book, so balances grow roughly linearly past a few thousand dollars. The dollar amounts compare the filters. The backtest also overstates live results by about 2.4¢ per contract (section 5); the ¢ per contract column is the size-free measure.

2. Train, test, holdout: the playground recipe

The same steps as the Prior Labs playground, with one change that matters for markets: the split is by time. A random split would let the model learn from the future. The table it runs on is public and playground-ready (data/tabpfn_ready/kxbtc15m_features.csv).

model = TabPFNClassifier(model_path="v3.5_default", n_estimators=8)
model.fit(train[features], train["target"])          # Jun 7 – Aug 2
p_test = model.predict_proba(test[features])[:, 1]   # Aug 3 – Sep 6: pick the trading margin, once
p_hold = model.predict_proba(holdout[features])[:, 1]  # Sep 7 – Oct 3: scored once

Kalshi keeps only about two months of history, so this record exists only because it was captured live. It is also messy: crossed books, stale quotes, outages and a collector rewrite on 30 July. Every price used for modelling is taken at a single instant and checked against Kalshi's own 1-minute candles.

4. The markets

A KXBTC15M contract asks whether BTC will finish a 15-minute window higher than it started; KXBTCD asks whether BTC will be above a strike at the top of the hour. Both pay $1 and settle on the CF Benchmarks BRTI index. Buying costs the ask plus a fee of 0.07 × price × (1 − price), 1.75¢ at 50¢.

The backtest picks the same trades as live. The gap is price: live orders arrive about 7 s later and pay a little more, so the backtest overstates profit by about 2.4¢ per contract.

6. Public benchmark: generic indicators, anyone can rerun it

Every model gets the same 24 textbook indicators and the same 5,000 most recent rows, in weekly walk-forward tests (9 weeks on the 15-minute market, 6 on the hourly ladder). The six classic models are tuned; TabPFN is not. Lower log loss means better probabilities.

Sanity checks

A planted signal was found by Logistic regression and TabPFN-3.5 (LightGBM missed it with 5,000 rows). With labels drawn from the market price itself, no model found fake skill.

7. Conclusion

  • TabPFN-3.5 works as a practical model on messy, real market data: refit weekly on a few thousand rows, no tuning, one CPU.
  • It ranked my strategy's signals best of the models tested, and its veto on my real live trades kept the trades that made money (+6.33¢ vs -0.31¢ per contract).
  • It did not escape a regime change on its own: in July it kept trading a signal that had stopped working. Sizing matters as much as the model, and half-Kelly stakes protected every filter.
  • On generic indicators it is at or near the top of seven learners, and nothing beats the market price on prediction error.

About the data

The repo publishes everything needed to rerun the public benchmark, and the scores, decisions and outcomes behind section 1. The full dataset (about 245 million rows of tape, order book, spot and settlement index since 2026-03-21) is mine and is the basis of my trading strategies, so it is not public. If you would like to work with it, open an issue on the repo or reach me through my GitHub profile.

Reproduce

git clone https://github.com/Cloblak/tab-trader && cd tab-trader
uv sync
export TABPFN_TOKEN=...      # free at https://ux.priorlabs.ai
make quick                   # one test week per market, about 10 minutes on CPU
make benchmark               # everything (a few hours)
make analyze report          # rebuild this page

Earlier research of mine looked at some of section 1's weeks, so a live forward test is the next step. TabPFN-3.5's open weights are licensed for evaluation; live trading with them needs a commercial licence or the Prior Labs API.
